nodes.description: The Marburg virus glycoprotein (GP), acting largely through its mucin-like domain, shields and downregulates cell-surface molecules, rounds and detaches adherent cells, and damages endothelial cells, disrupting monolayer barrier function. This is the Marburg-specific driver of the endothelial activation and damage step of the viral-hemorrhagic-fever syndrome.

nodes.description: Marburg virus replicates to high titre and reaches the vascular endothelium and the mononuclear phagocyte compartment. Filovirus entry into these target cells requires the endosomal cholesterol transporter NPC1 after glycoprotein-mediated attachment and fusion. The high systemic viral burden presented to the vasculature and myeloid cells initiates the vascular and hemostatic arms of disease.
